children: Malaysia's exports could continue to remain resilient in 1Q 2027, supported by sustained AI-driven demand for electrical and electronic products and stronger energy shipments, says CGS International economist Mas Aida Che Mansor in a note. Global semiconductor sales are forecast to grow 29% in 2027. Domestic electrical and electronics capacity utilization of 87.7% also points to continued shipment growth despite rising base effects, she reckons. Petroleum and liquefied natural gas exports should provide additional support, driven by regional demand and resilient manufacturing activity in China and the Asean region. However, a sharper slowdown in the U.S. or China, weaker crude oil prices and rising trade protectionism could weigh on shipments, she adds. (yingxian.wong@wsj.com)
